quote: Louis Massett offers a lively insight into the ethos of Catholic traditionalism. His memoir is warm and funny in parts, poignant and soulful in others. I wanted to leap into the pages and hug the hurting souls. Massett recalls many of the events I was aware of as a seminarian in Winona, Minnesota, and I can identify with elements of his journey. I heartily recommend his book.
A memoir the Church needs now.
Traddyland is a powerful, beautifully written memoir that delivers far more than a personal story. It's an unflinching and sometimes tragic exploration of faith, identity, trust, betrayal.

Readers will feel his painful struggle reconciling his belief in Christ and the goodness of Catholicism juxtaposed with the radicalism of Traddyist Catholic members of the Society of Saint Pius X that broke away from the Catholic Church in 1988.
Massett does a wonderful job in this book, painting a vivid picture of his life growing up in a splinter group of staunch traditional Catholics.
